questions.question: Someone browses on their phone on Monday and then buys on a laptop the following week. How do you actually know that's the same person and not two people?
questions.why_it_matters: The prospect is asking whether cross-device stitching is deterministic, probabilistic, or magic, and the SC has to explain the linking mechanism without overpromising.

questions.question: We share tablets across a household and we have customer service reps logging into accounts on behalf of customers. What stops four different people from getting collapsed into one profile?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the collapsed-graph objection. The SC is being asked whether there are configurable controls to prevent over-merging, not just a description of how merging works.

questions.question: We already have our own loyalty ID that we trust more than anything else. Do we have to adopt Adobe's identifiers or can we keep ours as the primary key?
questions.why_it_matters: The customer is protecting an existing golden record. The SC has to show that custom namespaces make their ID first-class rather than subordinate to an Adobe cookie ID.

questions.question: Some of our B2B contacts have dozens of identifiers attached to them. Is there a point where this falls over, and what happens when we hit it?
questions.why_it_matters: A scale and limits question disguised as a curiosity question. The SC needs the actual guardrail numbers and the failure behaviour, because getting this wrong surfaces in year two.

questions.question: When our data team says a customer got merged wrong, can we actually open up that one customer and see why the system linked them?
questions.why_it_matters: This is a trust and auditability question. The SC is being asked whether identity is a debuggable system or an opaque one.

questions.question: If someone abandons a cart, how fast can we actually do something about it? Minutes, or are we waiting until the next morning?
questions.why_it_matters: The prospect is testing whether 'real-time' in the product name is marketing or measurable, and which rule types actually qualify for streaming evaluation.

questions.question: Can the website change what it shows during the same visit, or does the person have to come back tomorrow for the personalization to kick in?
questions.why_it_matters: Same-page personalization is a different architecture from streaming segmentation, and conflating the two is the fastest way for an SC to lose credibility in a technical evaluation.

questions.question: Our top five percent of spenders are worth chasing. Can this find us more people who look like them, or do we have to define that ourselves?
questions.why_it_matters: The customer is asking whether modelled expansion is native or requires a separate data science investment, which changes the business case and the entitlement conversation.

questions.question: Our campaign managers don't write SQL and we can't put every audience request through engineering. What can a marketer actually build on their own?
questions.why_it_matters: Time-to-value hinges on self-service. The SC is being asked whether the platform reduces the engineering queue or just relocates it.

questions.question: We sell to companies, not individuals. Can we build a list of accounts rather than a list of people?
questions.why_it_matters: A B2B qualifier. The SC needs to know whether account-level audiences are a real object or a workaround built on person profiles.

questions.question: Our CRM says one address and the call centre system says another. When they disagree, which one ends up on the profile?
questions.why_it_matters: Conflict resolution is the question behind most data quality objections, and the answer is a configurable policy rather than a fixed rule.

questions.question: How long do you hang on to all this behavioural data? Our retention policy says two years and I need to know whether that's enforceable here.
questions.why_it_matters: A retention question that is really a legal sign-off blocker. The SC needs to show event expiry is configurable per dataset, not a global setting.

questions.question: Do we have to rebuild our entire data model to fit your format before we can get any value out of this?
questions.why_it_matters: The single biggest perceived implementation cost. The SC has to explain classes, field groups, and incremental modelling well enough to shrink the estimate.

questions.question: We handle health and financial information. Is there anywhere in this system that data is explicitly not supposed to go?
questions.why_it_matters: A regulated-industry gate. The SC is being asked for the documented position on SPI and PII in the data model, not a reassurance.

questions.question: When we push an audience to Meta, what actually leaves our environment? Are we shipping raw email addresses over to them?
questions.why_it_matters: A privacy and security review question. The SC has to be precise about hashing and which identities are exported per destination type.

questions.question: Our loyalty vendor isn't on your connector list and they're not going to build an integration for us. Are we stuck?
questions.why_it_matters: The catalog-gap objection. The SC needs to show there is a supported path to a custom destination and be honest about who builds and maintains it.

questions.question: All our customer data already sits in Snowflake and our data team does not want a second copy of it. What does connecting that actually look like?
questions.why_it_matters: The data-duplication objection from the warehouse team. The SC needs the specifics of the Snowflake connector rather than a generic 'we integrate with everything'.

questions.question: Our events happen all day. Can we send them as they happen instead of dropping a file every night?
questions.why_it_matters: Streaming ingestion is the prerequisite for every real-time use case the prospect just got excited about, so the SC has to make the setup sound concrete.

questions.question: Legal will not let us send email addresses to ad platforms. Can the system stop that from happening, or are we relying on people not making mistakes?
questions.why_it_matters: The customer is asking for technical enforcement rather than process, which is what gets governance teams to sign off on activation.

questions.question: When a customer asks us to delete them, how do we prove to a regulator that it actually happened everywhere?
questions.why_it_matters: A DSR audit-trail question. The SC has to separate what Privacy Service handles automatically from what the customer still owns.

out_of_scope.question: What would Real-Time CDP cost us for about 12 million profiles and four sandboxes?
We're also looking at Salesforce Data Cloud. Which one resolves identity better?
When are you shipping native clean room support? Our media team needs it by Q2.
Our CMO heard Nike runs on this. Can you walk me through how they configured their identity graph?
Can you pull up the redlines our legal team sent back on the MSA last week?
